To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we can generate high quality playlists using a combination of user specific listening patterns (which we refer to as a user model), and a domain model that encodes the taxonomy and popularity information, 2) the user and domain models can be learned from data using Bayesian inference and 3) the importance of the user and domain model varies depending on the seed~artist, and 4) the user and seed~artists are correlated with the importance of the domain model.

1) A hierarchical Bayesian model that incorporates a number of different information sources can be used to generate playlists that are personalized for individual users; 2) The hierarchical model allows for a number of different sources of information to be used in the generation process, including a taxonomy of artists; 3) The hierarchical model also allows for the importance of each source of information to be learned automatically, and to vary based on the user and seed~artists.
